item.title: OpenAI audit finds about 30% of SWE-Bench Pro coding tasks broken due to test and prompt issues, raising concerns about AI model evaluation accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI conducted a detailed audit of SWE-Bench Pro, a widely used coding benchmark, and found that approximately 30% of its tasks are flawed. These issues include overly strict tests, underspecified prompts, low test coverage, and misleading instructions, which can misrepresent AI model capabilities and affect safety and deployment decisions. The audit involved an automated data quality pipeline, agent-assisted reviews, and a human annotation campaign with experienced software engineers. The findings highlight the challenges in creating fair and reliable benchmarks for evaluating AI coding performance and suggest that developers should carefully interpret results from SWE-Bench Pro.

item.title: Developer describes experiencing burnout from extensive daily use of large language models due to repetitive errors and writing styles [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A developer who frequently uses large language models (LLMs) like Claude Code and Codex for coding tasks reports feeling burnout after a year of heavy daily interaction. While LLMs have increased productivity and exposed the developer to new approaches, repetitive mistakes, hallucinations, and uniform writing styles have led to frustration and a sense of fatigue with AI-generated content. The developer's workflow involves designing code, describing it to LLMs, reviewing their output, and then writing code, often relying on LLMs for unsupervised code generation frameworks. Despite appreciating the benefits, the persistent patterns of errors and stylistic quirks in LLM outputs have become wearing, and the developer is uncertain how to address this growing dissatisfaction.

item.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5, its most advanced model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, offering faster speeds and higher token efficiency [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: SpaceXAI has introduced Grok 4.5, its smartest AI model designed to excel in coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work. Trained on extensive datasets covering coding, science, engineering, and math, Grok 4.5 delivers intelligent and efficient reasoning, outperforming comparable models in real engineering tasks. It is available today in Grok Build, Cursor, and via the SpaceXAI API, with EU availability expected in mid-July. The model was trained using tens of thousands of NVIDIA GB300 GPUs with advanced data curation and reinforcement learning techniques focused on multi-step software engineering and technical tasks. Grok 4.5 operates at 80 transactions per second and offers roughly twice the token efficiency of leading models, reducing costs and speeding up results. It also supports complex office work, including building Excel models and creating PowerPoint and Word content, and is priced competitively at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live, a full-duplex voice model enabling natural, continuous human-AI conversations with background delegation to GPT-5.5 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a new generation of voice models designed for more natural and fluid human-AI interaction by allowing simultaneous listening and speaking. GPT-Live can engage in back-and-forth dialogue, use conversational cues, and delegate complex tasks like web search and reasoning to GPT-5.5 running in the background, maintaining conversation flow. GPT-Live improves on previous voice AI systems by using a full-duplex architecture that processes input and output continuously rather than in discrete turns, reducing interruptions and latency. OpenAI is rolling out two versions, GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1 mini, to ChatGPT users globally and plans to offer API access to developers and enterprises soon. Human evaluations show GPT-Live outperforms earlier voice modes in conversational naturalness and task performance.

item.title: AI shifts software rewrite economics by favoring codebases with clear, consistent patterns and popular tech stacks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Advancements in AI are changing the economics of software rewrites by making the quality of generated code dependent on the training data and the context provided by the existing codebase. Codebases using popular technologies benefit from AI's familiarity with established patterns, while proprietary or legacy systems require more effort and cost to teach AI their unique structures. This dynamic encourages rewrites not only to modernize technology stacks but also to create codebases optimized for AI assistance, potentially giving companies a competitive advantage in development speed and output quality.

item.title: TryAI.dev compares Grok 4.5, GPT-5.5, and Claude models by having them build identical interactive HTML apps to evaluate coding and animation capabilities [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: TryAI.dev conducted a build-off test where Grok 4.5, GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Fable 5 were each given the same three prompts to create self-contained interactive HTML apps without external libraries or network calls. The models were evaluated on a 3D Rubik's Cube animation, a particle gravity sandbox, and a playable Breakout game, with results tested live in browsers and performance measured in speed and cost. Claude models excelled in the 3D Rubik's Cube task, producing fully animated and correctly colored cubes on the first try, while Grok 4.5 required a retry and GPT-5.5 produced a less complete cube. GPT-5.5 delivered the most visually engaging particle sandbox, and all models produced polished Breakout games. Grok 4.5 stood out for speed and cost efficiency, streaming tokens roughly twice as fast as others and being the cheapest to run, though it struggled initially with the most complex task. The comparison highlights trade-offs between raw coding ability, visual output quality, and operational efficiency among leading AI coding models, providing insights for developers choosing models based on workload demands and application complexity.

item.title: Microsoft releases Flint, a visualization language designed for AI agents [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Microsoft has launched Flint, a new visualization language aimed at improving the way AI agents are represented and understood. The tool is intended to help developers and researchers create clearer visualizations of AI agent behaviors and interactions. Flint is available on Microsoft's GitHub pages and has sparked discussion among developers interested in AI visualization techniques. The release provides a resource for those working on AI systems to better communicate complex agent dynamics through visual means.

item.title: Report: US AI data center expansion slowed by electric grid interconnection delays amid rising power demand [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A major bottleneck in the AI buildout is the limited capacity of the US electric grid to connect new data centers and manufacturing plants, despite sufficient overall electricity supply. Projects like OpenAI and Softbank's $40 billion Stargate campus in Texas require massive power, but grid operators face backlogs and outdated interconnection processes that delay approvals and upgrades. The growing demand for electricity from AI data centers, semiconductor fabs, and battery plants is straining transmission infrastructure, causing congestion and higher costs. Industry leaders including Nvidia, Meta, and OpenAI have highlighted power availability as a key constraint on AI growth. Experts say grid modernization and more flexible interconnection rules are needed to support the expanding AI and electrification economy.

item.title: Researchers propose multimodal audio sentiment analysis integrating multilingual ASR transcripts with cross-modal transformers and knowledge distillation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose a multimodal approach to audio sentiment analysis that combines automatically generated speech transcripts and their machine-translated versions with audio features using cross-modal transformers. They further distill knowledge from this multimodal model into a unimodal audio-only model to improve performance without increasing inference costs. Experiments on a large-scale dataset show that incorporating multilingual textual information significantly enhances sentiment polarity classification accuracy. An ablation study confirms the benefits of both automatic transcripts and translations, and the team has publicly released their code to facilitate reproduction of results.

item.title: Researchers evaluate retrieval-augmented generation for public health question answering using UK government guidance, showing hybrid retrieval improves accuracy and smaller models can match larger ones [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers extended PubHealthBench, a public health question answering benchmark with 7,929 questions from UK government guidance, to a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) setting. They systematically compared dense, sparse, and hybrid retrieval methods across various embedding models and corpus variants, finding that hybrid retrieval consistently enhanced recall and ranking quality. Providing retrieved context improved multiple-choice accuracy across diverse large language models (LLMs), enabling smaller open-weight models to perform as well as or better than larger models without retrieval. The study introduced a rubric-based LLM-as-a-judge framework to assess free-form answers on faithfulness, completeness, clarity, and factual consistency, validated against human annotations. Agreement was strongest for faithfulness and completeness, while factual consistency and clarity showed less reliable alignment, suggesting caution in interpreting these metrics at scale. Overall, the results highlight retrieval quality and context selection as key factors for reliable public health question answering and offer practical guidance for building and evaluating RAG systems grounded in official guidance.

item.title: Researchers propose self-critical masked language model using reinforcement learning to generate e-commerce ad headlines outperforming human and existing AI methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a programmatic approach to generate product advertising headlines for e-commerce sites using a Transformer-based masked language model enhanced with reinforcement learning policy gradient methods. Their model creates headlines conditioned on multiple products simultaneously and has demonstrated superior performance compared to existing Transformer and LSTM-based methods in both overlap metrics and quality audits. The generated headlines also surpassed human-submitted ones in grammar and creative quality according to audit evaluations.

item.title: Researchers propose gradient-based speech-to-text alignment method applicable to any differentiable ASR model, including speech LLMs, without training or model changes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce a generic gradient-based method for speech-to-text alignment that identifies word boundaries by analyzing gradients of token log probabilities with respect to input audio. This approach works across various ASR model families, including CTC, transducer, attention-based encoder-decoders, and speech large language models, without requiring additional training or model modifications. The method aligns on the input audio grid, offering finer temporal precision than traditional encoder frame grids. The method was evaluated on sixteen models from four families using both read and spontaneous speech datasets, comparing its performance to native or attention-based alignments. Results show the gradient-based alignment is usable for all tested models, generally trailing strong native aligners but outperforming them where native alignments are weak, such as in streaming models. The main limitation is the computational cost, as it requires one backward pass per token during alignment.

item.title: Agon introduces competitive cross-model reinforcement learning where two models grade each other's reasoning to improve problem-solving performance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Agon is a new reinforcement learning approach that trains two competing models to grade each other's reasoning by alternately drafting and reviewing solutions to the same problem. This method implicitly evaluates reasoning during training without explicit process labels or reward models, encouraging models to out-reason their rivals. At inference, the models operate as a two-stage cascade, with one drafting and the other answering after reading the draft. On the challenging DeepMath dataset using Qwen3 models, Agon doubles the pass@1 accuracy compared to GRPO and significantly outperforms an untrained Mixture-of-Agents baseline. The approach also generalizes to competitive programming code and other model families like Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4. Currently, the models communicate via text, with future work aiming to enable joint reasoning in latent space.

item.title: Researchers propose Co-LMLM, a continuous-query limited memory language model using vector-keyed knowledge bases to improve factual precision and perplexity [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Co-LMLM, a limited memory language model that externalizes factual knowledge to a knowledge base with continuous vector keys paired with textual values, enabling flexible queries and human-readable retrieval. Trained on Wikipedia and FineWeb-Edu datasets, Co-LMLM outperforms prior limited memory and vanilla language models in perplexity and factual accuracy across multiple scales. At a 360 million parameter scale, it achieves lower perplexity than models trained on 40 times more data and matches or exceeds performance of models like gpt-4o-mini and Claude Sonnet 4.5 on SimpleQA verification.

item.title: SciReasoner introduces a multimodal foundation model for native structural reasoning across proteins, molecules, and crystals, achieving state-of-the-art results on 67 of 86 benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: SciReasoner is a new AI model designed to interpret structure-property relationships in biology, chemistry, and materials science by preserving native structural information and applying scientific constraints. It discretizes coordinates, topologies, and periodic connectivities into a unified vocabulary, enabling interpretable reasoning across proteins, small molecules, and inorganic crystals. The model improves Gene Ontology prediction for low-homology proteins, increases retrosynthesis accuracy in chemistry, and distinguishes elemental and compound phases in materials science. Across 86 benchmarks, SciReasoner achieved state-of-the-art performance on 67 tasks, with expert evaluations favoring its reasoning traces over those of leading large language models in 98% of cases.

item.title: LiveOIBench benchmarks 34 large language models on 403 expert-curated Informatics Olympiad problems, finding GPT-5 ranks below top human contestants [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: LiveOIBench introduces a large-scale competitive programming benchmark with 403 expert-designed problems from 72 contests across 14 Informatics Olympiads between 2023 and 2025, featuring extensive test cases and a fully offline evaluation system. The benchmark enables direct comparison of large language models (LLMs) to elite human contestants and is continuously updated to minimize data contamination. Testing 34 popular LLMs, GPT-5 achieved the 81.76th percentile, while the best open-weight model reached the 60th percentile, indicating that current models still lag behind top human performers. Reasoning analyses suggest that effective models focus on precise problem analysis rather than broad exploration. The benchmark's leaderboard, code, and data are publicly available for further research and evaluation.

item.title: Researchers propose Direct On-Policy Distillation to transfer reinforcement learning gains from smaller to larger language models, improving performance without costly rollouts [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Direct On-Policy Distillation (Direct-OPD), a method that reuses reinforcement learning (RL) policy shifts learned by smaller, cheaper models to enhance stronger target models without running expensive RL on them. This approach compares a weak teacher model's post-RL policy to its pre-RL state, using the difference as an implicit reward signal for the stronger student model. Empirical results show Direct-OPD improves a 1.7 billion parameter model's performance on AIME 2024 from 48.3% to 58.3% in four hours using eight A100 GPUs, outperforming direct RL training and enabling sequential policy improvements. The study demonstrates that RL outcomes can be effectively transferred across model scales as implicit rewards rather than just final policies to imitate.

item.title: AgentLens launches a benchmark for evaluating coding agents by reviewing their full operational trajectories with formal verification and LLM-generated explanations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: AgentLens introduces a new benchmark for interactive code agents that evaluates their entire operational trajectory, including instruction following, tool usage, error recovery, and communication, rather than just task success. It combines formal verification with large language model-generated trajectory reviews and side-by-side comparisons to provide detailed explanations of performance scores. The benchmark is open source and supports diagnosing model behavior, comparing agent versions, and detecting regressions in production evaluation pipelines.

item.title: Researchers present a sampling-complexity theory showing in-context search improves large language model reasoning when reflections identify early errors, validated on real models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent theoretical study models in-context search in large language models as approximate inference over reasoning traces, where self-reflection updates the model's posterior to improve problem-solving success. The research finds that when reflections reliably detect early mistakes, in-context search can exponentially improve success rates using only a polynomial number of sequential attempts, even for problems with very low zero-shot pass rates. If reflections fail to localize errors, sequential attempts offer no advantage over parallel sampling. The study also shows these improvements can be learned through cross-entropy training and align with reinforcement learning policies. Key predictions were confirmed using real large reasoning models.

item.title: Researchers propose EvoSOP framework for self-evolving LLM agents that synthesize atomic actions into reusable Standard Operating Procedures to improve task success and efficiency [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce EvoSOP, a framework that enables large language model (LLM) agents to evolve by combining basic atomic actions into higher-order Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that encapsulate multi-step logic. This approach addresses limitations of static toolsets that require agents to repeatedly solve low-level tasks, increasing failure rates and reasoning overhead. EvoSOP extracts SOPs from execution trajectories and iteratively optimizes the toolset through construction, merging, evaluation, and pruning. Experiments show that EvoSOP significantly improves task success rates and reduces interaction rounds compared to baseline methods, fostering more reliable and efficient tool-use patterns and offering a scalable path for developing self-evolving agents.

item.title: Researchers introduce Physics-Audited Agentic SciML workflow to verify surrogate models against physics constraints in scientific machine learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose Physics-Audited Agentic Scientific Machine Learning (PA-SciML), a verification-first workflow that evaluates surrogate models generated by large language model agents against physics requirements such as boundary conditions and causality. The workflow fixes a scoring evaluator before model search, applies machine-checkable physics checks to each candidate, and identifies high-violation cases without relying on reference solutions, reporting surrogates as verified only if they pass these checks. In computational solid mechanics examples, PA-SciML selected surrogates with lower validation errors than error-only baselines while passing physics checks. Notably, in transient elastodynamics, a baseline model with similar mean error failed a causality check by responding to future loading history, whereas the PA-SciML-selected surrogate passed all physics verifications. This approach emphasizes per-candidate physics evidence over aggregate error scores to improve model reliability in scientific machine learning.

item.title: Researchers find biased judges disable skill retirement in self-evolving AI agents by allowing false passes, undermining evaluation without visible impact on aggregate metrics [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A study shows that self-evolving AI agents rely on unbiased judges to retire ineffective skills by detecting failures, but biased judges that falsely pass failures can silently disable this skill retirement mechanism. This failure occurs beyond a sharp threshold of false-pass bias and is not detectable through aggregate evaluation metrics, posing a behavioral safety concern rather than a performance issue. The researchers conducted a corrupted-reward analysis and behavioral experiments using a reference-free report-writing testbed with code-generation cross-checks, demonstrating that symmetric noise does not impair skill retirement, but false-pass bias does. This mechanism failure is universal across domains and failure rates, except for near-zero-false-pass, verifier-like graders. The study proposes a defect-injection audit to help operators identify whether their judge falls on the safe or unsafe side of this threshold before deployment.

item.title: Researchers find reinforcement learning post-training composes primitive skills into higher-level reasoning strategies in a Transformer model [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers studied whether reinforcement learning (RL) post-training simply amplifies existing primitive skills or composes them into new strategies using a Transformer pretrained on symbol-rewrite chains. They found that RL enabled the model to solve held-out reasoning problems rarely solved by pretraining alone, reorganizing primitive skills into sequential and parallel composed procedures that form a stable repertoire. Compared to rejection fine-tuning, RL focused exploration on valid reusable structures rather than invalid shortcuts, and the emergence of compositional strategies depended on pretraining organizing primitive competence into reduction procedures that RL could compress. This work shows RL can build reliable higher-level reasoning strategies from weak procedural ingredients provided by a base model.

item.title: TriRoute introduces a unified controller for joint adaptive attention, expert selection, and KV-cache allocation in language models, improving efficiency and robustness across models from 160M to 1.3B parameters [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: TriRoute presents a single lightweight controller that jointly manages attention resolution, expert selection, and KV-cache bit-width for every token at each layer in decoder-only language models. This approach coordinates decisions across these three axes, which are typically handled independently, to optimize compute and memory costs while preserving model quality. The controller is trained end-to-end with a Lagrangian budget constraint and addresses training challenges like routing-collapse cascades through normalization and balancing losses. Evaluated on models ranging from 160 million to 1.3 billion parameters, TriRoute outperforms the best independent combinations of Mixture-of-Depths, Mixture-of-Experts, and KV-cache quantization at matched inference FLOPs and memory usage. It also better maintains robustness on rare tokens, code, and arithmetic tasks that are often degraded by pure perplexity optimization. Analysis shows the controller allocates full attention and high-precision caching to important tokens such as sentence-initial words, rare subwords, and named entities, while routing common function words more cheaply.

item.title: NEST introduces a regime-oriented mixture-of-experts framework to address dataset-level distribution shifts in multivariate time-series forecasting [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: NEST is a new framework designed to improve long-term forecasting accuracy in complex systems by explicitly modeling dataset-level distribution shifts caused by distinct operational regimes. It uses a two-phase dense mixture-of-experts architecture that partitions datasets into regimes via unsupervised clustering and applies a regime-oriented router to assign expert weights, enabling experts to specialize in regime-specific dynamics. The approach was evaluated on diverse benchmarks including network traffic and physical phenomena, consistently achieving state-of-the-art performance. NEST's design allows it to capture evolving system states more effectively than methods focusing only on local temporal shifts, and its code and datasets have been made publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers propose D2PO framework to optimize diffusion samplers using dynamic preference alignment, improving perceptual quality under low-NFE constraints [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce D2PO (Dynamic Direct Preference Optimization), a framework that optimizes diffusion sampling policies by reformulating sampler training as a preference-based alignment problem. This approach addresses limitations of existing student-teacher regression methods that often sacrifice fine texture details when mimicking high-NFE teachers, leading to misalignment with perceptual quality. D2PO models sampling policies as energy-based models and uses dynamic preferences that improve iteratively, replacing static teacher supervision with a self-improving refinement process. The framework derives a novel energy formulation from pretrained score networks to evaluate preferences in perturbed spaces capturing both structural consistency and fine details. Extensive experiments show that D2PO better aligns diffusion samplers with perceptual quality, unlocking the potential of high-quality teachers and outperforming conventional regression-based schedulers, especially under low number of function evaluations (NFE) constraints.

item.title: Researchers propose deep reinforcement learning framework for multi-objective portfolio optimization using risk measures and realistic market models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose a deep reinforcement learning framework called MORP-DRL for multi-objective portfolio optimization that jointly optimizes expected return and downside risk using variance, CVaR, and EVaR risk measures. The approach models asset returns with GARCH(1,1), Extreme Value Theory, and a t-copula dependence structure, generating scenarios via quasi-Monte Carlo simulation, and incorporates practical constraints such as transaction costs and portfolio bounds. The framework uses Proximal Policy Optimization and is benchmarked against NSGA-II, demonstrating competitive risk-return performance and reduced downside risk during market stress across ten global equity indices in pre-COVID, COVID, and post-COVID regimes. MORP-DRL also shows scalability to high-dimensional portfolio settings, addressing limitations of static optimization methods in capturing sequential decision making and tail risk.

item.title: Researchers present STAGformer, a spatio-temporal agent graph transformer for efficient bike-sharing demand forecasting with linear complexity [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: STAGformer is a new model designed to improve station-level demand forecasting in bike-sharing systems by capturing complex spatio-temporal dependencies across large urban networks. It uses a two-step agent attention mechanism to aggregate and distribute global information efficiently, reducing computational costs while modeling long-range interactions. The model integrates four modules: a spatio-temporal encoder combining dynamic node features with external factors like weather and points of interest, a graph propagation module for spatial aggregation, a temporal convolution module for local patterns, and the agent attention module for global dependencies. Experiments on NYC Citi-Bike and Chicago Divvy-Bike datasets show STAGformer outperforms existing methods across multiple prediction horizons, with ablation studies highlighting the importance of the agent attention mechanism for global modeling.

item.title: FedEAS introduces entropy-adaptive synthetic data generation budgets to reduce label skew in federated learning, cutting computation by 94.1% while maintaining accuracy gains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: FedEAS is a new policy designed to address label skew in federated learning by assigning each client a per-class synthetic data generation budget based on its local label distribution entropy. This approach determines both the amount of data each client generates and the allocation of samples, allowing the total generation budget to emerge from client-specific needs rather than a fixed global limit. FedEAS achieves nearly the same accuracy improvements as full class balancing but with a 94.1% reduction in generation budget, outperforming uniform allocation by up to 18.82% on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets.

item.title: Inertia-1 introduces an open framework for wearable motion foundation models using over 18 million hours of global accelerometer data to study data, model, and training choices [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Inertia-1 presents a comprehensive, open exploration of wearable motion foundation models by analyzing massive accelerometer datasets totaling more than 18.2 million hours from global sources. The study examines various factors including sensor modality, device placement, sampling rate, model architectures, and training objectives to understand how these influence model performance across diverse tasks. The framework evaluates models on 15 datasets covering human activity recognition, freezing-of-gait detection, and disease prediction, revealing insights for building models that generalize well across different sensing conditions and tasks. Inertia-1 offers state-of-the-art methods and serves as a practical resource for wearable motion representation learning.

item.title: Researchers propose LLM-guided Task-Semantic Field Factorization to improve industrial process forecasting accuracy by up to 25.5%, adding minimal overhead [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Task-Semantic Field Factorization (TSF), a framework guided by large language models (LLMs) that incorporates semantic information from process documents into time-series forecasting models for industrial processes. TSF uses LLMs offline to build semantic fields from task protocols and variable documents, while online training and inference rely on conventional time-series backbones enhanced by activated variable semantics within each numerical window. TSF addresses challenges in industrial forecasting such as scarce labeled data and frequent operating regime changes by enabling models to adapt to different prediction targets and shifts. Evaluations on multiple complex industrial forecasting and soft-sensing tasks show TSF reduces mean absolute error by an average of 6.4%, with a maximum reduction of 25.5%, while adding only 1.8 to 3.0 thousand parameters and less than 0.008 milliseconds per step of inference overhead, demonstrating its lightweight deployment potential and measurable forecasting gains across various backbones and semantic generators.

item.title: Researchers propose ROAM framework using LLM reasoning to adapt frozen specialist industrial models to new scenarios without retraining, reducing error by over 20% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Reasoning-Driven Open Adaptation for Specialist Models (ROAM), a framework that leverages large language model (LLM) world knowledge and reasoning to adapt frozen specialist models to unseen scenarios without retraining. ROAM confines corrections to a low-dimensional latent space and fuses LLM-generated scenario judgments with online observations under a probabilistic framework, suppressing unreliable corrections and reverting to the original model when evidence is insufficient. Experiments on mineral thickening and penicillin fermentation datasets demonstrate that ROAM reduces mean absolute error by over 20% in major shift scenarios with minimal additional parameters and low computational overhead. These results suggest that LLM reasoning can provide a conservative adaptation signal for industrial models already deployed in service, addressing challenges like sensor drift and regime changes without costly retraining.

item.title: Researchers introduce cross-trajectory chimera interventions to separate roles of weight magnitude and direction in neural network grokking [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers developed cross-trajectory chimera interventions to test which properties of partially trained neural networks transfer across independently trained runs. By recombining the norm and direction components of weight vectors from different training seeds and continuing training on modular-arithmetic tasks, they found that direction carries a transferable, donor-specific circuit identity, while norm mainly affects training delay without encoding identity. Implanting a donor's direction into a recipient's norm consistently shifted the recipient's network to the donor's solution, with the transfer exhibiting a threshold behavior predicted by the recipient's norm.

item.title: Researchers propose Dynamic-in-Few-Step framework combining dynamic computation and few-step distillation to accelerate video diffusion models, achieving 30x speedup with preserved quality [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce a post-training acceleration framework called Dynamic-in-Few-Step that integrates dynamic structural sparsification into the distillation process of video diffusion models (VDMs). This approach transforms a pre-trained VDM into a compact, step-specific Mixture-of-Models (MoM), optimizing denoising steps and model sparsity jointly to reduce computational costs while maintaining generation quality. The method addresses training instability with a Progressive Training Strategy and Output Rollout Mechanism and includes a specialized inference engine for efficient deployment. Applied to the Wan-14B model, it reduces 24% of per-step FLOPs beyond 4-step distillation, resulting in a 1.2x wall-clock speed gain and an overall 30x speedup compared to the original 50-step model.

item.title: Researchers find grounding tests in specifications improves LLM-generated code correctness by up to 38 percentage points across multiple models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A study shows that large language models (LLMs) generate more correct code when their tests are explicitly grounded in a specification of expected behavior, rather than merely existing. By controlling for tester, test budget, and repair loop, researchers demonstrated that providing a checklist of specification rules to the tester increased correct code generation by 38 percentage points across three Claude model tiers and 36 points on a held-out set. The improvement stems from grounding rather than test quantity, as doubling test budgets or combining multiple ungrounded test suites yielded smaller gains.

item.title: Researchers audit grokking representation metrics, finding embedding compression lags generalization by over 10,000 steps and effective rank overstates convergence in MLPs and transformers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed neural network embeddings on modular arithmetic tasks and found that compression continues for tens of thousands of steps after the network has already generalized. They discovered that measuring effective rank at the grokking transition overestimates the converged value by 3-5 times in multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and by 1.3-1.5 times in transformers trained to convergence, with compression lagging accuracy transitions significantly. The study includes an audit method that separates the onset of compression from its progression, identifies censoring effects, excludes boundary cells that do not fully generalize, and verifies that reference floors have plateaued, with the researchers releasing their code and toolkit for further use.

item.title: Researchers find that the dimensionality of the training objective determines how much of a task's predictive structure a world model represents, with scalar value signals capturing only a one-dimensional projection [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study on DreamerV3 models shows that the extent to which a learned world model captures the predictive features needed for a task depends on the dimensionality of the objective it is trained against, rather than model capacity or observations. The researchers demonstrate that scalar value signals install only a one-dimensional projection of the task's closure, while increasing the objective's dimensionality allows the model to represent more predictive directions. This finding suggests that value equivalence in world models is dimensional, with the common single-reward objective representing just the rank-one corner of the task's structure.

item.title: Researchers introduce Diffusion Semi-Relaxed Fused Gromov-Wasserstein for robust graph matching, improving accuracy and clustering under noise and partial observations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Diffusion Semi-Relaxed Fused Gromov-Wasserstein (DsrFGW), a new method for graph comparison that integrates node features and structural connectivity using optimal transport and diffusion processes. This approach addresses limitations of traditional Gromov-Wasserstein methods, particularly in handling sparse, noisy, or partially observed graphs by capturing both local and global structural patterns while reducing sensitivity to missing edges. An extensive evaluation on 36 synthetic graph matching tasks of varying difficulty showed that DsrFGW consistently outperforms previous semi-relaxed fused Gromov-Wasserstein methods, with accuracy improvements up to 20 percentage points and significant gains in clustering quality measured by the Adjusted Rand Index. The method adapts diffusion scales to problem difficulty and improves clustering quality in 92% of tasks even under severe noise, establishing it as a robust framework for graph comparison under structural uncertainty.

item.title: Researchers introduce SPEAR, a Python-based simulator that enhances photorealistic embodied AI research by enabling control of Unreal Engine applications with over 14,000 functions and rendering at 73 FPS [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: SPEAR is a new Python library designed to improve photorealistic simulators for embodied AI by connecting to any Unreal Engine (UE) application through a modular plugin system. It offers an order-of-magnitude increase in programmable functionality with over 14,000 UE functions accessible and can render 1920x1080 photorealistic images at 73 frames per second directly into NumPy arrays, significantly faster than existing UE plugins. SPEAR also provides unique ground truth image modalities such as non-diffuse intrinsic image decomposition and material IDs, which are not available in other UE-based simulators. The simulator introduces a high-level programming model that allows users to specify complex graphs of UE tasks with arbitrary data dependencies, executing them deterministically within a single UE frame. Demonstrations include controlling multiple embodied agents with different action spaces, rendering city-scale environments, manipulating procedural content generation, synchronizing multi-view images of human faces, co-simulating with the MuJoCo physics engine, and editing scenes using natural language commands via an AI coding assistant.

item.title: Review of Vision Language Action Models for Bimanual Manipulation and Unmanned Aerial Robotics, Covering 183 Studies from 2017 to 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This review examines Vision Language Action (VLA) models that integrate visual perception, natural language understanding, and action generation to enable robots to perform tasks from camera images and instructions. It focuses on bimanual manipulation, where two robotic arms coordinate complex movements, and unmanned aerial robotics, where drones manage thrust, attitude, and gripper commands under strict constraints. The study covers 183 contributions from 2017 to 2026, analyzing VLA architectures, training methods, action representations, and coordination strategies across both domains. The review highlights how techniques developed for bimanual VLAs transfer to unmanned aerial systems and identifies fourteen research directions spanning VLA architectures, UAV navigation and control, language grounding, and cross-cutting issues such as memory and world models. It provides a comprehensive overview of the state of the art and emerging challenges in applying VLA models to complex robotic manipulation and aerial tasks.

item.title: Researchers develop AirPASS, an alternating optimization framework for over-the-air federated learning using multi-waveguide pinching antenna systems to improve device selection and beamforming [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This paper presents AirPASS, a framework designed to enhance over-the-air federated learning (AirFL) in wireless systems equipped with multi-waveguide pinching antenna systems (PASS). AirPASS jointly optimizes device selection, receive beamforming, and antenna placement to maximize selected devices while controlling aggregation distortion, addressing the nonconvex challenges of these coupled variables. The framework employs a homotopy-Riemannian margin-consolidation method for device selection and beamforming under fixed antenna configurations, alongside a homotopy-assisted geometry optimization for antenna positioning. Experimental results demonstrate that AirPASS outperforms traditional co-located MIMO baselines, approaches the performance of ideal federated averaging (FedAvg), and offers a favorable tradeoff between performance and complexity compared to other scheduling methods.

item.title: Researchers apply knowledge distillation to improve efficiency of deep learning models for time series classification across FCN, Inception, and ConvTran architectures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers investigate knowledge distillation (KD) to transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models for time series classification, aiming to reduce computational demands while maintaining performance. They evaluate KD on three architectures-Fully Convolutional Network (FCN), Inception, and transformer-based ConvTran-using the UCR Archive benchmark datasets. Their results show that KD benefits student models of intermediate complexity most effectively, with the distilled FCN reducing parameters by a factor of 38, the Inception student achieving near-teacher performance with 42% fewer parameters, and the ConvTran student with two attention heads showing the largest improvement. The team has released their implementation to support further research and reproducibility.

item.title: Study finds verification-based signals from large language model judges best predict correctness of AI-generated multi-table text-to-SQL queries [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated various signals to predict correctness of AI-generated SQL queries, defined as producing the same result as human-written references, on challenging multi-table benchmarks BIRD and Spider. They found that black-box signals like self-consistency and schema relevance achieved moderate accuracy (AUROC around 0.61 to 0.68), while verification-based signals from large language model judges improved performance to 0.72-0.78 AUROC, with ensembles reaching 0.82 AUROC and supporting reliable selective prediction. The study also explored training fine-tuned verifiers, which performed well in-distribution (0.77 to 0.79 AUROC) but showed degraded accuracy (around 0.66 AUROC) on unseen database schemas. Attempts to improve cross-schema generalization through scaling, schema diversity, rationale distillation, and cross-benchmark training were unsuccessful. The results suggest that reasoning-based signals from large frozen models currently offer the best generalization for correctness uncertainty in text-to-SQL tasks.

item.title: Study identifies key factors that improve lightweight reinforcement learning agents in imperfect-information card games using a fixed expert benchmark [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers developed a strong, fixed rule-based expert for Gin Rummy to serve as a benchmark for evaluating lightweight reinforcement learning agents, which typically outperform random opponents but struggle against stronger competition. They found that techniques such as trust region updates, targeted rewards, a curriculum of tougher opponents, warm starting, and checkpoint retention improved agent performance, raising a self-play champion's win rate against the expert from about 30 to 36 percent. The study also tested various approaches that did not enhance performance, including reward shaping, learned state embeddings, imitation learning, and using a large language model opponent, citing issues with training speed and scalability. Comparing different neural network architectures showed that increasing model capacity had limited effect, suggesting information constraints rather than network size limit agent strength. The findings were validated on Leduc Hold'em, and the researchers released a game-agnostic training package for lightweight agents without expert training.

item.title: Researchers analyze Stochastic-Oracle Turing Machines under cached and fresh oracle response schemes, identifying performance limits and error reduction rates in AI-augmented computation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This paper studies the Stochastic-Oracle Turing Machine (SOTM) framework, which models AI-augmented computation as a probabilistic Turing machine interacting with an oracle providing context-dependent responses. It compares two oracle-response schemes: cached-response, where each query receives one reusable response, and fresh-response, where each call returns an independent response. The study identifies performance ceilings imposed by cached responses and shows that fresh responses can improve accuracy by accumulating independent evidence over repeated calls. The analysis includes error probability reduction at the Chernoff rate in binary single-informative-query cases and characterizes output quality through query-count bounds and majority-based amplification. The results clarify how response reuse, transcript information, and access to scoring functions influence what an SOTM can compute and the associated token costs.

item.title: Researchers propose LoCA, a spatially-aware low-rank convolutional adaptation method for vision foundation models that decouples channel and spatial adaptation to improve parameter-efficient fine-tuning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Low-Rank Convolutional Adaptation (LoCA), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework designed for vision foundation models that preserves spatial topology by decoupling channel and spatial adaptation in convolutional kernels. LoCA uses low-rank channel adaptation and refines spatial bases via singular value decomposition to maintain pre-trained spatial priors. Experimental results demonstrate that LoCA achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance across tasks including fine-grained classification, domain-generalized semantic segmentation, and generative benchmarks, addressing limitations of previous low-rank adaptation methods that treated convolutional kernels as 2D matrices and disrupted spatial information.

item.title: Researchers propose CAGI, a cluster-aware generative imputation framework that jointly optimizes clustering and missing data recovery using a Partition-Guide-Restore strategy and GANs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Missing data is common in real-world datasets that often contain latent subgroups with distinct distributions, posing challenges for effective imputation. Researchers introduce CAGI (Cluster-Aware Generative Imputation), which addresses the circular dependency between subgroup identification and data completion by co-optimizing clustering and imputation through an iterative feedback loop using dynamic cluster assignments as priors for a Generative Adversarial Network. CAGI employs a multi-level optimization combining instance-level reconstruction with distribution-level regularization to maintain distributional stability. Experiments on 14 benchmark datasets against 15 baselines demonstrate CAGI's superior performance in recovering missing data while preserving subgroup structures. The source code is publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers introduce a multifactor scoring system to evaluate large language model responses, assessing accuracy, conciseness, factual consistency, readability, and coherence with a GUI, tested on the TruthfulQA dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a comprehensive evaluation framework for large language models (LLMs) that integrates multiple factors including accuracy, conciseness, factual consistency, readability, and coherence. This system includes a graphical user interface for visualizing results and was applied to the TruthfulQA dataset, revealing strengths in reasoning but challenges with complex facts and ambiguities. The framework aims to provide a transparent and adaptable method for assessing LLM capabilities beyond traditional single-metric evaluations. While currently focused on English tasks, the approach is intended to extend to multilingual contexts, offering new directions for knowledge engineering and model improvement.

item.title: Survey examines dual-use risks and defensive strategies of large language models and generative AI in cybersecurity, highlighting AI-generated malware growth and explainability challenges [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: This paper surveys the dual-use applications of large language models (LLMs) and generative AI in cybersecurity, detailing their roles in both automated defense and sophisticated attacks. It highlights a rapid increase in LLM-generated malware, which accounted for an estimated 50% of detected threats by 2025, up from 2% in 2021, underscoring the need for advanced security frameworks in 2026. The survey reviews over 70 academic and industry sources, covering topics such as zero-day detection, DevSecOps, federated learning, synthetic content analysis, and explainable AI (XAI). It draws insights from real-world case studies involving platforms like Google Play Protect, Microsoft Defender, AWS, Apple App Store, OpenAI Plugin Stores, Hugging Face Spaces, and GitHub, as well as emerging initiatives like the SAFE Framework and AI-driven anomaly detection. The authors conclude with recommendations for responsible LLM deployment, including model watermarking, adversarial defense, and cross-industry collaboration, aiming to guide researchers, engineers, and security leaders in managing AI-driven cybersecurity challenges.

item.title: Researchers propose hybrid least squares/gradient descent method to accelerate MIONet training using multilinear optimization and matrix factorization techniques [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose an efficient hybrid least squares/gradient descent (LSGD) method to accelerate training of MIONets, a neural network architecture combining multiple branch networks and a trunk network. The method generalizes previous LSGD approaches for DeepONets by optimizing last layer parameters of each branch network using alternating least squares and solving large linear systems with matrix factorization techniques such as Kronecker and Khatri-Rao products. The approach supports general $L^2$ loss functions with regularization terms applied to the last layer parameters of each branch, allowing linear operators on the MIONet output within each loss term. This method aims to improve training efficiency for complex multilinear neural network models by leveraging structured optimization and matrix decomposition strategies.

item.title: Physics-guided spatiotemporal neural models for fuel density prediction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.06999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a physics-guided machine learning (PGML) framework for fuel density prediction, integrating physics constraints and domain knowledge into deep learning models to enhance model accuracy and stability. We explore three deep learning architectures -- ConvLSTM, Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator (AFNONet), and Video Vision Transformer (ViViT) -- to model the spatiotemporal evolution of fuel density. Our approach incorporates differentiable physics-informed terms in the loss function, including a mass-conserving fuel transport term and a rate-of-spread estimation. Experimental results, averaged across multiple independent trials, demonstrate that the proposed PGML framework outperforms purely data-driven baselines without physics constraints in both accuracy and stability. This framework enables computationally efficient, physically plausible fire forecasting to support adaptive prescribed burn management.

item.title: Multimodal Spatiotemporal-Frequency Fusion with Peak Enhancement for Cellular Traffic Forecasting [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate forecasting of cellular network traffic is essential for network planning, resource allocation, and quality-of-service assurance in modern mobile communication systems. Real-world traffic often exhibits bursty endogenous dynamics and disturbances triggered by external urban events, which makes reliable prediction highly challenging. Most existing spatiotemporal traffic forecasting methods primarily focus on intrinsic traffic patterns or structural relationships within a single modality, and rarely model burst behavior together with exogenous contextual signals. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{MSPF-Net}, a multimodal cellular traffic forecasting framework that integrates external contextual information. Specifically, MSPF-Net consists of a Spatiotemporal-Frequency Traffic Encoder for capturing temporal, spatial, and spectral traffic patterns, a Peak Enhancement Module for extracting burst-aware representations of sudden spikes, a News Context Representation Module for encoding urban news streams into exogenous contextual embeddings, and a Dynamic Fusion Prediction Module for adaptively integrating these heterogeneous signals to generate forecasts. Experiments on the Milano, Trento, and LTE traffic datasets demonstrate that jointly modeling traffic dynamics, burst patterns, and news contextual signals can effectively improve forecasting performance.

item.title: Latent graph encoding of multimodal neuroimaging features with generative AI architectures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While generative models enable encoding of complex neuroimaging data for feature generation and reconstruction, developing optimal architectural frameworks with appropriate encoding and latent space processes is crucial for studying structural and functional properties of the brain. We design a multimodal generative framework for structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features through systematic evaluation of encoding strategies, latent multimodal fusion, and generative model selection. Using structural gray matter volume (GMV) and static functional network connectivity (sFNC) features from a large neuroimaging dataset, we analyze generative frameworks involving variational autoencoders (VAEs), transformers, generative adversarial networks (GANs), and diffusion models. Architectures that employ modality-aware graph encoding of functional connectivity into a lower-dimensional latent space outperform vectorized encoders or direct data space approaches. The proposed multimodal graph VAE (gMMVAE) surpasses alternative generative variants across multiple metrics for generation fidelity, reconstruction quality, efficiency, and latent space discriminability, highlighting its potential for robust multimodal neuroimaging analysis.

item.title: Gimitest: A Comprehensive Tool for Testing Reinforcement Learning Policies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies can be unsafe and vulnerable to attacks. Ensuring their reliability is often a pain point as existing automated testing methods target only selected environments, testing scenarios, and RL algorithms. To address this, we propose a comprehensive framework for testing single- and multi-agent RL policies under varying conditions. Our implementation of this framework, Gimitest, is an open-source tool that supports various gym frameworks and allows for modifications of their integrated components. This article describes the framework and details Gimitest's functionality and architecture. It showcases its effectiveness in testing multiple RL policies in environments such as the official Farama Gymnasium and PettingZoo.

item.title: Intrinsic Green's Learning: Supervised Learning on Manifolds via Inverse PDE [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Intrinsic Green's Learning (IGL), a framework that models a target function on a manifold as the solution to a linear PDE whose source term is learned from data. Rather than approximating the target directly, IGL learns a source and integrates it against a Green's kernel. An encoder discovers a low-dimensional coordinate chart on the manifold where both the source and the kernel decompose as low-rank tensors, collapsing a high-dimensional integral into independent one-dimensional integrals with cost linear in the intrinsic dimension. A two-stage algorithm separates coordinate discovery from source fitting, a near-convex linear solve, preventing the dimensional collapse of joint training. Learnable gates on each coordinate automatically discover the intrinsic dimension of the manifold. We validate IGL on synthetic manifolds and on MNIST, where it simultaneously achieves near-optimal classification and automatic recovery of the intrinsic dimension.

item.title: On the Principles of Deep Feedforward ReLU Networks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The architecture of deep feedforward neural networks is ubiquitous in deep learning, either as a whole system or as a subnetwork of other architectures, and thus its mechanism is a key ingredient of the black box of neural networks. On the basis of the simplest two-layer ReLU network, this paper systematically studies the mechanism of deep feedforward ReLU networks with multiple hidden layers and successfully explains the training solution obtained by the back-propagation algorithm. The concept of a path, especially in terms of the relationships between paths, plays a central role in uncovering the mystery of the black box. It is shown that a unit of a deep ReLU network can form a piecewise linear manifold to divide the input space, instead of a hyperplane of the two-layer case. How to efficiently use the hidden-layer units to produce both linear functions and partitions of the input space is also a central problem. The principles of a two-layer ReLU network can be generalized to the deeper case to a large extent, such as multiple strict partial orders and continuity restriction. The combination of the basic and simple principles proposed can yield complicated instantiations including the training solutions, and in this sense the black box of deep feedforward ReLU networks is revealed.

item.title: Riemannian Geometry for Pre-trained Language Model Embeddings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the geometric structure of pre-trained language model embeddings matters for interpretability and safety. We ask whether sentence-level classification signal lives in the Riemannian geometry of contextual token embeddings, and probe it by extracting per-token pullback metrics from a learned encoder's analytical Jacobian and aggregating them with the Fr\'echet mean on the symmetric positive definite (SPD) manifold; we call this procedure Riemannian Mean Pooling (RMP). Across three datasets with non-trivial linguistic structure (CoLA, CREAK, RTE), RMP outperforms Euclidean mean pooling, while on FEVER-Symmetric, a benchmark constructed to remove annotation-driven lexical artifacts, the method correctly stays at chance. Ablations show that a randomly initialised encoder combined with Fr\'echet aggregation already beats Euclidean pooling on two of the three signal-bearing datasets, localising the source of the gain to the geometric aggregation rather than to learned manifold structure; the trained encoder contributes additional signal specifically on CREAK, the most knowledge-heavy of the three signal-bearing datasets.

item.title: Complexity-Budgeted, Interaction-Aware Interpretable Model for Tabular Data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inherently interpretable classifiers for tabular data typically rely on sparse features, rules, or patterns that users can inspect directly. The marginal feature-screening step common to these methods can discard variables whose predictive value emerges only through joint configurations with other variables. We present Interaction Aware Interpretable Machine Learning (IAIML), a framework that addresses this limitation through three coordinated mechanisms: adaptive per-feature discretization, finite-grid pairwise interaction scoring, and a partitioned explanation budget. Detected interactions are routed through one of two strategies: relaxing the screening filter so that interaction-supported variables enter the pattern search, or constructing explicit pair terms for a sparse downstream classifier. On a 40-dataset panel comprising 24 real-world tabular benchmarks and 16 synthetic interaction stress tests, evaluated under nested cross-validation, IAIML achieves mean AUC within 1.4 points of tuned gradient-boosted ensembles while requiring roughly 14--28 times fewer fitted explanation components. On datasets with strong pairwise interaction structure and low marginal signal, IAIML outperforms all baselines. Among compact interpretable methods, IAIML is comparable to RuleFit in AUC and component count and is less expensive to tune. EBM obtains a small but significant AUC advantage across the full panel, with a substantially larger lookup-table footprint. Performance degrades on datasets requiring higher-order interactions beyond the pairwise scope. Component-isolated ablations confirm that adaptive discretization and interaction-aware admission each contribute incrementally. These results support IAIML as a compact, interaction-aware framework appropriate for settings where bounded explanation size and controlled treatment of feature interactions are design requirements.

item.title: Multiplication Beyond Groups: Stratified Fourier Mechanisms in Transformer Circuits [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformers have demonstrated a remarkable ability to learn algorithmic reasoning, yet mechanistic analyses have mostly focused on globally invertible operations such as cyclic addition and group composition. In this work, we investigate how small transformers learn modular integer multiplication over composite moduli, a fundamentally non-invertible operation due to the presence of zero-divisors. We propose the monoid extension: a localized generalization of Group Composition via Representation (GCR) that suggests the learned computation does not rely on a single global representation space. Instead, the model partitions the input space into local hierarchical algebraic regions, where group-like structure survives and Fourier mechanisms can be applied. In transformers trained on square-free modular multiplication, we find that embeddings organize around these regions, attention exhibits class-sensitive routing and low-rank write directions, and local character features explain a large fraction of the model's output logits. Our results suggest that representation-theoretic mechanisms previously identified for group operations can extend beyond groups to more general structures.

item.title: Entropy Pacing Policy Optimization for Multi-Task Agentic Reinforcement Learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent breakthroughs of Reinforcement Learning (RL) have highlighted its potential for complex agentic Large Language Model (LLM) tasks. However, existing efforts largely focus on single-task settings, whereas real-world deployment necessitates a generalist agent capable of solving multiple tasks simultaneously. In this work, we identify a critical yet underexplored phenomenon in multi-task agentic RL: different tasks can exhibit exploration-exploitation pace mismatch. Specifically, easier tasks may converge early to low-entropy policies that hinder learning on harder tasks, while harder tasks can, in turn, push easier tasks back toward high-entropy exploration. This back-and-forth interaction creates inter-task entropy crossovers and frequent entropy spikes. Inspired by this observation, we introduce Entropy Pacing Policy Optimization (EPPO) for multi-task agentic LLMs, which coordinates entropy across tasks to stabilize multi-task optimization. At the core of EPPO is a task-wise dynamic clipping mechanism that replaces the fixed clipping threshold in Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a task entropy-aware adaptive bound, tightening updates for over-confident tasks while relaxing them for under-explored ones. Experiments on the multi-task agentic benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed EPPO yields results superior to its counterparts.

item.title: Predicting LLM Safety Before Release by Simulating Deployment [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pre-deployment safety evaluations aim to inform the downstream risks of releasing a new AI model. Yet most evaluations provide limited evidence about how often undesired model behavior will occur in deployment: they generally have insufficient coverage, are unrepresentative, and are generally recognizable as tests. To address these concerns, we study a simple way to simulate a model deployment: starting from de-identified conversations from a previous model deployment, we hold fixed the initial conversation prefix and regenerate the next response using a candidate model. The resulting responses can then both be audited for novel misalignments and used to estimate the prevalence of model misbehavior before deployment. We evaluate deployment simulation across four GPT-5-series deployments, using registered, outcome-blinded predictions for GPT-5.4 and retrospective analyses of three earlier releases. We find that deployment simulation produces informative estimates of post-deployment misbehavior rates and outperforms baselines based on adversarially selected production data; its evaluation-awareness point estimates were also much closer to production traffic than those from traditional evaluations. We also identify the realism of tool resampling as a central challenge for further improving predictions and share results suggesting that this challenge is surmountable even in complex tool-use settings. Finally, we show that deployment simulation can be seeded from public chat datasets and remain informative about production misbehavior rates, suggesting a path for external researchers to run deployment-grounded evaluations without access to private production logs. Overall, deployment simulation helps evaluators forecast how language models will behave in the real world and supports more quantitative assessment of deployment risk.

item.title: Validate the Dream Before You Trust Its Verdict: Admissibility for World-Model Simulators [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07196v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Across robotics, World Models (WMs) are increasingly used to evaluate action policies by simulating the consequences of actions in an imagined world, and returning a success or safety verdict. Yet a verdict is only as trustworthy as the WM that produced it, and the WM itself needs to be certified. In video-generation WMs, fidelity metrics such as Fr\'echet Video Distance (FVD) reward visual realism, but ignore whether the world responds correctly to the policy's actions, including those unseen in training. Classical simulation-based validation assumes a trusted simulator evaluating an untrusted policy, whereas generative WMs are themselves unverified learned artifacts. Hence, we argue that any WM used as a test oracle must first be accredited before its verdicts can serve as evidence. Building on credibility practices from safety-critical simulation, including Verification, Validation & Accreditation (VV&A), Safety of the Intended Functionality (SOTIF), and scenario-based testing standards, we define an admissibility ladder (L0-L4) that a WM must climb before its closed-loop verdicts are accepted as assurance evidence. Our framework is embodiment-agnostic, and is instantiated in autonomous driving (AD), where assurance methods for traditional simulation are most mature. Applied to two driving WMs, the lower rungs reveal a reversal: the model that ranks higher on visual generation quality (L0) ranks lower on action-following (L1-L2), so visual fidelity does not predict the action-robustness a closed-loop verdict depends on.

item.title: Vision Foundation Models in Radiology: A Scoping Review of Data, Methodology, Evaluation and Clinical Translation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07219v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision foundation models (VFMs) are increasingly being developed for radiological imaging, yet their definition, development and evaluation remain heterogeneous. We conducted a PRISMAScR scoping review of peer-reviewed studies published between January 2017 and March 2026 describing foundation models trained exclusively on radiological imaging data. Sixty-seven studies were included and mapped across three pillars: data scale and heterogeneity, architectural and pretraining scalability, and downstream transferability and generalization. Datasets primarily covered brain MRI, thoracoabdominal CT, and chest X-ray, ranging from fewer than 100,000 samples to multi-million-image cohorts. Transformer-based architectures and self-supervised pretraining predominated, particularly masked image modeling, contrastive learning and multi-stage approaches. Evaluation focused mainly on segmentation and classification, whereas cross-center, cross-scanner, anatomical and modality-shift validation was inconsistently reported. Alignment with FUTURE-AI principles was uneven. Overall, radiology-specific VFMs show promising transferability, but clinical translation remains constrained by limited data representativeness, heterogeneous benchmarks, incomplete reporting and insufficient deployment-oriented evaluation.

item.title: DiPhon: Diffusion on Graphons for Scalable Graph Generation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion models represent a leading paradigm for graph generation, with notable impact in domains such as molecular design. Yet, scaling these models to large graphs remains an open problem. We approach this question in the dense-graph setting through the lens of graphons, the size-agnostic limit objects of dense graph sequences, to study how structural graph statistics behave across node-size scales. This perspective leads to DiPhon, a diffusion framework for size-scalable graph generation. Specifically, we formulate a continuous diffusion process on the graphon space via a Jacobi stochastic differential equation (SDE), and propose DiPhon, a discretized graph-level process that mimics these dynamics on finite graphs. We further derive the corresponding reverse-time process, which requires access to the marginal score. For the Jacobi process, this score interestingly admits a tractable form, which we estimate from data via graph denoising and plug into the reverse process to generate graph samples. We prove that DiPhon matches exactly the first moment of the marginal distributions induced by the continuous graphon process, and approximates the second moment up to a closed-form discrepancy. Thus, DiPhon inherits key size-agnostic statistical properties of the graphon dynamics, providing a principled route toward scalable graph generation. Empirically, we demonstrate this scalability by training on small graphs and generating progressively larger graphs at inference time, without retraining, while preserving their core topological properties.

item.title: ORCAID: Oblique Rule-Based Continuous-Action Interpretation for Deep RL Policies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Explainability remains a key issue in reinforcement learning (RL). Distilling an interpretable policy from an agent trained in a complex environment is particularly challenging when the action space is continuous. We introduce ORCAID, a novel method for extracting interpretable rule-based policies from RL agents operating in mixed continuous-discrete environments with continuous action spaces. Our main contribution is an efficient oblique decision tree training algorithm that partitions the state space by hyperplanes and fits local linear models. The key idea lies in a three-stage split search: efficient random initialization, local refinement, and backward elimination. Finally, adjacent leaves are merged to yield a concise set of interpretable rules describing a given deep RL policy. We evaluate ORCAID across multiple RL environments, demonstrating that the extracted rule-based policies maintain strong performance with a low number of parameters and can even be used to improve the performance of the original deep RL policy.

item.title: FMMVCC: Fuzzy Mamba-based Multi-View Contrastive Clustering for Univariate Time Series [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In many realistic scenarios, large volumes of time series data are generated with limited or expensive annotations. This limitation makes supervised learning methods difficult to apply and leads to the use of unsupervised approaches capable of discovering meaningful structures directly from raw data. Clustering therefore plays a crucial role in organizing time series into groups that share similar temporal patterns, enabling exploratory analysis and downstream tasks without requiring manual labeling. However, existing deep clustering methods often struggle to capture long-range temporal dependencies or rely on architectures with high computational cost. This paper introduces FMMVCC, a Mamba-based deep clustering framework for time series that leverages state space sequence modeling to efficiently learn temporal representations with linear complexity. Additionally, it utilizes multi-view self-supervised learning with temporal masking and augmentations. Experimental evaluation in 15 benchmark datasets proves that FMMVCC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving the best overall performance in 29 of 60 total metric evaluations and the highest average rank in all tested scenarios.

item.title: Bayesian Optimization of Genetic Algorithm Hyperparameters in a Multi-Fidelity Framework for Efficient Lattice Material Design [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study presents a multi-fidelity framework for the systematic optimization of genetic algorithm (GA) hyperparameters. The framework integrates three fidelity levels: high-fidelity Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) homogenization for validation, a medium-fidelity 3D convolutional neural network surrogate for rapid property evaluation, and a low-fidelity Gaussian process (GP) surrogate within a Bayesian optimization (BO) framework to guide the hyperparameter search. Various acquisition functions are evaluated, with logNEI achieving the best performance by effectively accounting for the noise inherent in GA evaluations. The proposed framework identifies hyperparameter configurations that enable a 25-generation GA run to achieve elastic modulus values comparable to those obtained in a full 75-generation optimization. Furthermore, introducing a penalized BO objective significantly reduces the number of required lattices with only minor decreases in absolute achieved elastic modulus, revealing a practical trade-off between performance and the number of structures that must be evaluated. High-fidelity FFT validation verifies the effectiveness of the surrogate-driven optimization strategy. The optimized hyperparameters allow for rapid convergence, eliminate the need for lattice mutation, and reduce the overall computational cost by 24% (from 225 to 171 hours) while preserving mechanical performance. These results demonstrate the potential of multi-fidelity optimization as an efficient and practical approach for GA hyperparameter tuning and future experimental lattice design studies.

item.title: Multimodal Voice Activity Projection for Turn-Taking in Social Robots with Voice-Activity-Related Pretrained Encoders [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07294v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Turn-taking prediction is a key requirement for social robots involved in human-human interaction, particularly in mediator settings, where the robot must anticipate conversational dynamics rather than merely react to pauses. This work presents a Multimodal Voice Activity Projection (MM-VAP) framework that extends the original audio-only VAP formulation to synchronized audio-visual inputs while preserving its self-supervised future-projection objective. The proposed approach builds on pretrained audio-visual backbones originally optimized for speech-related tasks and adapts them through Low-Rank Adaptation to the multimodal turn-taking problem. After independent speaker encoding, an inter-speaker attention stage models the relational dynamics required to project future voice activity. In addition, a semantic consistency loss is introduced to regularize the 256-state output space according to higher-level dialogue activity patterns. Experiments on NoXi and NoXi+J showed improvements over the current baselines, particularly for some turn-taking events. Additional evaluation on the Haru EDR corpus further supported the suitability of this direction for mediation-oriented human-robot interaction.
